text: Watch this little bottle shoot out a giant snake of foam.
It's called elephant toothpaste and it's pure chemistry.
The bottle holds strong hydrogen peroxide and a squirt of dish soap.
Peroxide falls apart into water and oxygen but on its own it's super slow.
So we pour in a helper that makes it go way faster.
The helper rips a peroxide apart then lets go and grabs the next one.
It never gets used up so it just keeps going.
All that oxygen gets trapped in the soap as millions of tiny bubbles.
The bubbles have nowhere to go but up and out.
It gets so hot the foam can steam.
That's why you need gloves and goggles for this one.
It looks like toothpaste for an elephant. Watch it again.
